subproblems.title: Domains G_{x,λ} = η_{x,λ}(B_2(0)): membership test ‖x + λv‖ < 2, openness, and B_2(0) ∪ closedBall 0 R ⊆ G_{x,λ} for admissible (x, λ) with λR ≤ 1 (parent steps 0(e), 4)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) and λ > 0, let η_{x,λ} := dilation x λ (so η_{x,λ}(u) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹u) and G := η_{x,λ}(B_2(0)), where B_2(0) is the open ball of radius 2 about 0. Then: (a) for every v ∈ ℝ^P, v ∈ G ⟺ ‖x + λ·v‖ < 2; (b) G is open; (c) if moreover λ ≤ 1 and ‖x‖ ≤ 1 − λ, then B_2(0) ⊆ G, and closedBall 0 R ⊆ G for every real R with λ·R ≤ 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → (∀ v : Euclid P, v ∈ dilation x lam '' ball 0 2 ↔ ‖x + lam • v‖ < 2) ∧ IsOpen (dilation x lam '' ball 0 2) ∧ (lam ≤ 1 → ‖x‖ ≤ 1 - lam → ball 0 2 ⊆ dilation x lam '' ball 0 2 ∧ ∀ R : ℝ, lam * R ≤ 1 → closedBall 0 R ⊆ dilation x lam '' ball 0 2)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 4 (domains; Simon 7.3.3, proof of 3.3(1), item (9): the members with lim λ_i = λ > 0 live on U_S = η_{x,λ}(U), chapter-07.txt lines 445–467) together with the membership equivalence of parent step 0(e) (v ∈ G_{x,λ} ⟺ x + λv ∈ B_2(0)). Both are proved here directly from the definition of dilation, since the parent's sibling ambient_calculus is not available to this child. The inclusion closedBall 0 R ⊆ G for λR ≤ 1 is the closed-ball form of the inclusion B_{1/λ}(0) ⊆ G_{x,λ} of parent step 4, which parent step 5c uses.
Notation: η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ and G := η(B_2(0)).
1. (Formula for η.) By definition, dilation x λ u = −(λ⁻¹•x) + dilationCLM P λ u, and dilationCLM P λ = λ⁻¹ • id, so dilationCLM P λ u = λ⁻¹•u. Hence η(u) = λ⁻¹•u − λ⁻¹•x = λ⁻¹•(u − x) for every u ∈ ℝ^P.
2. ((a), ⇒.) Let v ∈ G, say v = η(u) with u ∈ B_2(0), i.e. ‖u‖ < 2. By step 1, λ•v = λ•(λ⁻¹•(u − x)) = (λλ⁻¹)•(u − x) = u − x, because λ ≠ 0. Hence x + λ•v = u and ‖x + λ•v‖ = ‖u‖ < 2.
3. ((a), ⇐.) Let ‖x + λ•v‖ < 2 and put u := x + λ•v, so u ∈ B_2(0). By step 1, η(u) = λ⁻¹•((x + λ•v) − x) = λ⁻¹•(λ•v) = (λ⁻¹λ)•v = v. Hence v = η(u) ∈ G.
4. ((b).) By (a), G = {v ∈ ℝ^P : ‖x + λ•v‖ < 2}. The map v ↦ ‖x + λ•v‖ is continuous (the continuous affine map v ↦ x + λ•v followed by the norm), so G is the set where a continuous function is strictly less than the constant 2, which is open (isOpen_lt).
5. ((c), first inclusion.) Assume λ ≤ 1 and ‖x‖ ≤ 1 − λ, and let v ∈ B_2(0), i.e. ‖v‖ < 2. Since ‖λ•v‖ = |λ|·‖v‖ = λ‖v‖ (λ > 0), the triangle inequality gives ‖x + λ•v‖ ≤ ‖x‖ + λ‖v‖ < (1 − λ) + 2λ = 1 + λ ≤ 2; the strict inequality uses λ > 0 and ‖v‖ < 2, the last one uses λ ≤ 1. By (a), v ∈ G. Hence B_2(0) ⊆ G.
6. ((c), second inclusion.) Under the same assumptions let R ∈ ℝ with λR ≤ 1 and let v ∈ closedBall 0 R, i.e. ‖v‖ ≤ R. Then ‖x + λ•v‖ ≤ ‖x‖ + λ‖v‖ ≤ (1 − λ) + λR ≤ (1 − λ) + 1 = 2 − λ < 2, using λ ≥ 0 for λ‖v‖ ≤ λR, the hypothesis λR ≤ 1, and λ > 0 for the last step. By (a), v ∈ G. Hence closedBall 0 R ⊆ G. (If R < 0 the closed ball is empty; the computation covers this case as well.)
7. Steps 2–6 prove (a), (b) and (c). ∎
proof_key_steps: dilation x λ u = λ⁻¹•(u − x); its inverse is v ↦ x + λ•v.
This set is a strict sublevel set of a continuous function, hence open.
For λ ≤ 1 and ‖x‖ ≤ 1 − λ: ‖x + λv‖ ≤ 1 − λ + λ‖v‖ < 2 when ‖v‖ < 2, or when ‖v‖ ≤ R with λR ≤ 1.

subproblems.title: Finite positive total mass of the seed μ₀ and of every member μ₀^{x,λ}, and concentration of μ₀ on B_2(0) (parent steps 0(a)–(c), 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, z ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0 with μ(B_{2r}(z)) ≠ 0 and μ(B_{2r}(z)) ≠ ∞, and let μ₀ := ofReal(r⁻¹^n)•(μ⌞B_{2r}(z)).map(dilation z r). Then μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ 0, μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞ and μ₀(B_2(0)ᶜ) = 0; and for every x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 the measure μ₀^{x,λ} := ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x λ) satisfies μ₀^{x,λ}(ℝ^P) ≠ 0 and μ₀^{x,λ}(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ μ₀ : Measure (Euclid P)) (z : Euclid P) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → μ (ball z (2 * r)) ≠ 0 → μ (ball z (2 * r)) ≠ ∞ → μ₀ = ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) • (μ.restrict (ball z (2 * r))).map (dilation z r) → μ₀ univ ≠ 0 ∧ μ₀ univ ≠ ∞ ∧ μ₀ (ball (0 : Euclid P) 2)ᶜ = 0 ∧ ∀ (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → (ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation x lam)) univ ≠ 0 ∧ (ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation x lam)) univ ≠ ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent steps 0(a), 0(b), 0(c) and 3, with the needed facts of the parent's sibling ambient_calculus (parts (2) and (3); not available to this child) proved inline. The last two conclusions are exactly clause (3) of the parent; the first three are the properties of μ₀ used by parent steps 2 and 5.
Notation: B := B_{2r}(z) (open ball), η_{a,s} := dilation a s, m := μ(B) ∈ (0, ∞).
1. (Dilations act measurably.) For a ∈ ℝ^P and s ∈ ℝ, η_{a,s}(u) = −(s⁻¹•a) + s⁻¹•u = s⁻¹•(u − a) (definition of dilation and dilationCLM). This map is continuous (affine), hence Borel measurable. Consequently, for every measure ν, every c ∈ [0, ∞] and every Borel set A: (c•ν.map(η_{a,s}))(A) = c·ν(η_{a,s}⁻¹(A)) (Measure.smul_apply, Measure.map_apply).
2. (Constants.) For s > 0 we have s⁻¹^n > 0, so ofReal(s⁻¹^n) ≠ 0; and ofReal(t) ≠ ∞ for every real t. In particular ofReal(r⁻¹^n) ∈ (0, ∞).
3. (Total mass of μ₀.) By step 1 with A = ℝ^P (η_{z,r}⁻¹(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P) and Measure.restrict_apply: μ₀(ℝ^P) = ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·(μ⌞B)(ℝ^P) = ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·μ(ℝ^P ∩ B) = ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·m. A product of two elements of (0, ∞) is ≠ 0 (mul_ne_zero) and ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.mul_ne_top). Hence μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ 0 and μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞.
4. (Concentration.) For every v ∈ ℝ^P: v ∈ η_{z,r}⁻¹(B_2(0)) ⟺ ‖r⁻¹•(v − z)‖ < 2 ⟺ r⁻¹‖v − z‖ < 2 ⟺ ‖v − z‖ < 2r (as r > 0) ⟺ v ∈ B. So η_{z,r}⁻¹(B_2(0)) = B and, taking complements, η_{z,r}⁻¹(B_2(0)ᶜ) = Bᶜ. The set B_2(0)ᶜ is closed, hence Borel, and Bᶜ is Borel; so by step 1 and Measure.restrict_apply, μ₀(B_2(0)ᶜ) = ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·μ(Bᶜ ∩ B) = ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·μ(∅) = 0.
5. (Members.) Let x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0. By step 1 with A = ℝ^P: μ₀^{x,λ}(ℝ^P) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·μ₀(η_{x,λ}⁻¹(ℝ^P)) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·μ₀(ℝ^P). By step 2 the first factor lies in (0, ∞) and by step 3 so does the second; hence μ₀^{x,λ}(ℝ^P) ≠ 0 and μ₀^{x,λ}(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: Dilations are continuous, so (c•ν.map η)(A) = c·ν(η⁻¹A) for Borel A.
μ₀(ℝ^P) = ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·μ(B_{2r}(z)) ∈ (0, ∞).
μ₀^{x,λ}(ℝ^P) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·μ₀(ℝ^P) ∈ (0, ∞).

subproblems.title: Support relation: for w ∈ B_2(0), w ∈ spt μ₀ ⟺ z + r·w ∈ spt μ (parent steps 0(d),(e), 1)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, z ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0 and μ₀ := ofReal(r⁻¹^n)•(μ⌞B_{2r}(z)).map(dilation z r). Then for every w ∈ B_2(0): (μ₀(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0) ⟺ (μ(B_ε(z + r·w)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ μ₀ : Measure (Euclid P)) (z : Euclid P) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → μ₀ = ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) • (μ.restrict (ball z (2 * r))).map (dilation z r) → ∀ w ∈ ball (0 : Euclid P) 2, (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → μ₀ (ball w ε) ≠ 0) ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → μ (ball (z + r • w) ε) ≠ 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1 (support relation), using the ball formula of parent steps 0(d),(e) in the special case x = 0, λ = 1, computed here directly for μ₀ (so parts (3) and (8) of the parent's sibling ambient_calculus, which is not available to this child, are not needed). This is clause (1) of the parent; the parent hypotheses n ≥ 1 and μ(B_{2r}(z)) ∈ (0, ∞) are not used.
Notation: B := B_{2r}(z), η := dilation z r, c := ofReal(r⁻¹^n).
1. (Dilation.) η(u) = −(r⁻¹•z) + r⁻¹•u = r⁻¹•(u − z) (definition of dilation and dilationCLM); η is continuous, hence Borel measurable.
2. (Preimages of balls.) For w ∈ ℝ^P and σ ∈ ℝ: η⁻¹(B_σ(w)) = B_{rσ}(z + r•w). Indeed r⁻¹•(v − z) − w = r⁻¹•(v − (z + r•w)), so ‖η(v) − w‖ = r⁻¹‖v − (z + r•w)‖, and this is < σ iff ‖v − (z + r•w)‖ < rσ, because r > 0.
3. (Ball formula.) For Borel A, μ₀(A) = c·(μ⌞B)(η⁻¹(A)) = c·μ(η⁻¹(A) ∩ B) (Measure.smul_apply, Measure.map_apply, Measure.restrict_apply). With step 2: μ₀(B_σ(w)) = c·μ(B_{rσ}(z + r•w) ∩ B) for every σ.
4. (Dropping the intersection.) Fix w ∈ B_2(0), so ‖w‖ < 2, and put δ := 2 − ‖w‖ > 0. For σ ≤ δ we have B_{rσ}(z + r•w) ⊆ B: if ‖v − (z + r•w)‖ < rσ, then ‖v − z‖ ≤ ‖v − (z + r•w)‖ + ‖r•w‖ < rσ + r‖w‖ ≤ r(2 − ‖w‖) + r‖w‖ = 2r. Hence μ₀(B_σ(w)) = c·μ(B_{rσ}(z + r•w)) for every σ ≤ δ.
5. (Constant.) c = ofReal(r⁻¹^n) ≠ 0 because r⁻¹^n > 0.
6. (⇒.) Assume μ₀(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0 and let ε' > 0. Put σ := min(δ, ε'/r) > 0. By step 4, c·μ(B_{rσ}(z + r•w)) = μ₀(B_σ(w)) ≠ 0, so μ(B_{rσ}(z + r•w)) ≠ 0 (a product with a zero factor is 0). Since σ ≤ ε'/r we have rσ ≤ ε', so B_{rσ}(z + r•w) ⊆ B_{ε'}(z + r•w), and monotonicity (measure_mono_null) gives μ(B_{ε'}(z + r•w)) ≠ 0.
7. (⇐.) Assume μ(B_ε(z + r•w)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0 and let ε > 0. Put σ := min(ε, δ) > 0. By step 4, μ₀(B_σ(w)) = c·μ(B_{rσ}(z + r•w)), and both factors are nonzero (step 5, and the assumption with the radius rσ > 0); hence μ₀(B_σ(w)) ≠ 0. Since σ ≤ ε, B_σ(w) ⊆ B_ε(w), and monotonicity gives μ₀(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0.
8. Steps 6 and 7 prove the equivalence for every w ∈ B_2(0). ∎
proof_key_steps: dilation z r⁻¹(B_σ(w)) = B_{rσ}(z + r•w), so μ₀(B_σ(w)) = ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·μ(B_{rσ}(z + r•w) ∩ B_{2r}(z)).
For σ ≤ 2 − ‖w‖ the ball B_{rσ}(z + r•w) lies in B_{2r}(z), so the intersection can be dropped.
With σ = min(2 − ‖w‖, ε/r) resp. min(ε, 2 − ‖w‖), nonvanishing transfers in both directions by monotonicity.

subproblems.title: Injectivity of (x, λ) ↦ ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x λ) for a finite nonzero μ₀ concentrated on B_2(0): total mass recovers λ, barycenter recovers x (parent step 2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, and let μ₀ be a measure on ℝ^P with μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ 0, μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞ and μ₀(B_2(0)ᶜ) = 0. If x, x' ∈ ℝ^P, λ, λ' > 0 and ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x λ) = ofReal(λ'⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x' λ'), then x = x' and λ = λ'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ₀ : Measure (Euclid P)), 1 ≤ n → μ₀ univ ≠ 0 → μ₀ univ ≠ ∞ → μ₀ (ball (0 : Euclid P) 2)ᶜ = 0 → ∀ (x x' : Euclid P) (lam lam' : ℝ), 0 < lam → 0 < lam' → ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation x lam) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam'⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation x' lam') → x = x' ∧ lam = lam'
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 2 (injectivity: total masses give λ = λ', barycenters give x = x'; the parent's departure [D1], members encoded by their weights). It is stated here for an arbitrary measure μ₀ with the three properties used in that step; for the parent's μ₀ these properties are parent step 0(b), i.e. the first three conclusions of the sibling total_mass, and clause (2) of the parent follows by instantiation.
Notation: η_{a,s} := dilation a s; ν_{a,s} := ofReal(s⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(η_{a,s}); c := μ₀(ℝ^P) ∈ (0, ∞).
1. (Dilations; total masses.) η_{a,s}(u) = −(s⁻¹•a) + s⁻¹•u = s⁻¹•(u − a), a continuous (affine), hence measurable, map. So ν_{a,s}(ℝ^P) = ofReal(s⁻¹^n)·μ₀(η_{a,s}⁻¹(ℝ^P)) = ofReal(s⁻¹^n)·c (Measure.smul_apply, Measure.map_apply).
2. (λ = λ'.) Evaluate the assumed equality ν_{x,λ} = ν_{x',λ'} at ℝ^P and use step 1: ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·c = ofReal(λ'⁻¹^n)·c. Since c ≠ 0 and c ≠ ∞, c cancels (ENNReal.mul_left_inj): ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) = ofReal(λ'⁻¹^n). Both λ⁻¹^n and λ'⁻¹^n are ≥ 0 and ofReal is injective on [0, ∞) (ENNReal.ofReal_eq_ofReal_iff), so λ⁻¹^n = λ'⁻¹^n. Since n ≠ 0 and λ⁻¹, λ'⁻¹ ≥ 0, t ↦ t^n is injective on [0, ∞) (pow_left_inj₀), so λ⁻¹ = λ'⁻¹ and λ = λ' (inv_injective). From now on λ' = λ, and the hypothesis reads ν_{x,λ} = ν_{x',λ}.
3. (μ₀ finite; the identity is integrable.) μ₀ is a finite measure because c ≠ ∞. The identity map v ↦ v is continuous, hence strongly measurable, and ‖v‖ ≤ 2 for μ₀-a.e. v: the exceptional set {v : ‖v‖ > 2} is contained in B_2(0)ᶜ, which is μ₀-null. The constant 2 is integrable for the finite measure μ₀, so the identity is μ₀-integrable (Integrable.mono' with integrable_const). Put b₀ := ∫ v dμ₀(v) ∈ ℝ^P and m₀ := (μ₀(ℝ^P)).toReal; m₀ ≠ 0 because c ∉ {0, ∞} (ENNReal.toReal_ne_zero).
4. (Barycenter of ν_{a,λ}.) For every a ∈ ℝ^P: ∫ v dν_{a,λ}(v) = (ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)).toReal • ∫ v d(μ₀.map η_{a,λ})(v) (integral_smul_measure) = λ⁻¹^n • ∫ η_{a,λ}(v) dμ₀(v) (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, since λ⁻¹^n ≥ 0; integral_map, valid since η_{a,λ} is measurable and the identity is continuous). Write η_{a,λ}(v) = −(λ⁻¹•a) + λ⁻¹•v. Both summands are μ₀-integrable (a constant for the finite measure μ₀, and λ⁻¹ times the integrable identity), so integral_add, integral_const (∫ const dμ₀ = (μ₀(ℝ^P)).toReal • const) and integral_smul give ∫ η_{a,λ} dμ₀ = m₀•(−(λ⁻¹•a)) + λ⁻¹•b₀. Hence ∫ v dν_{a,λ}(v) = λ⁻¹^n • (m₀•(−(λ⁻¹•a)) + λ⁻¹•b₀).
5. (x = x'.) Equal measures have equal integrals of the identity, so step 4 with a = x and a = x' gives λ⁻¹^n • (m₀•(−(λ⁻¹•x)) + λ⁻¹•b₀) = λ⁻¹^n • (m₀•(−(λ⁻¹•x')) + λ⁻¹•b₀). Cancel the nonzero scalar λ⁻¹^n (smul_right_injective), then the common summand λ⁻¹•b₀ (add_right_cancel), then the nonzero scalar m₀, then the negation (neg_injective), and finally the nonzero scalar λ⁻¹. This gives x = x'.
6. With step 2: x = x' and λ = λ'. ∎
proof_key_steps: Total mass: ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·μ₀(ℝ^P) = ofReal(λ'⁻¹^n)·μ₀(ℝ^P); cancelling μ₀(ℝ^P) ∈ (0, ∞) and injectivity of t ↦ t^n on [0, ∞) (n ≥ 1) give λ = λ'.
μ₀ is finite and |v| ≤ 2 μ₀-a.e., so the identity is μ₀-integrable; let b₀ be its integral and m₀ = μ₀(ℝ^P).toReal ≠ 0.
Barycenter: ∫ v d(ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map η_{a,λ}) = λ⁻¹^n•(m₀•(−λ⁻¹•a) + λ⁻¹•b₀).
Equating barycenters for a = x and a = x' and cancelling nonzero scalars gives x = x'.

subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let ν₁, ν₂ be measures on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra) such that ν₁(K) ≠ ∞ and ν₂(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and ∫ f dν₁ = ∫ f dν₂ for every continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support. Then ν₁ = ν₂.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν₁ ν₂ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν₁ K ≠ ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν₂ K ≠ ∞) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → ∫ x, f x ∂ν₁ = ∫ x, f x ∂ν₂) → ν₁ = ν₂
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 5b (basic fact (F6)) in the form recorded there as equivalent: finiteness on compact sets gives local finiteness and regularity on the σ-compact metric space ℝ^P, and regular measures are determined by their integrals of compactly supported continuous functions (Riesz–Markov–Kakutani uniqueness, Mathlib's Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported).
1. (Finite on compacts.) By hypothesis ν_i(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, i.e. ν_i is finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts), for i = 1, 2.
2. (Locally finite.) ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional normed space, hence locally compact: every point has a compact neighbourhood (a closed ball), which has finite ν_i-measure by step 1. So ν_i is locally finite (isLocallyFiniteMeasure_of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts).
3. (Regular.) ℝ^P is a σ-compact metric space carrying its Borel σ-algebra, and every locally finite measure on such a space is regular (Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure): it is outer regular (ν_i(A) = inf{ν_i(O) : O ⊇ A open} for Borel A) and inner regular on open sets with respect to compact sets (ν_i(O) = sup{ν_i(K) : K ⊆ O compact}).
4. (Agreement on compact sets.) Let K be compact and ε > 0. By outer regularity of ν₂ and ν₂(K) < ∞ there is an open V ⊇ K with ν₂(V) ≤ ν₂(K) + ε; in particular ν₂(V) < ∞. ℝ^P is locally compact Hausdorff, so by Urysohn's lemma there is a continuous f : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with compact support contained in V and f = 1 on K; f is bounded with compact support, hence integrable for both measures. Using 1_K ≤ f ≤ 1_V (as real functions), the finiteness of ν₁(K) and ν₂(V), and the hypothesis (f is continuous with compact support), we get in ℝ: ν₁(K).toReal = ∫ 1_K dν₁ ≤ ∫ f dν₁ = ∫ f dν₂ ≤ ∫ 1_V dν₂ = ν₂(V).toReal ≤ ν₂(K).toReal + ε. As ε > 0 is arbitrary, ν₁(K).toReal ≤ ν₂(K).toReal, and since both values are finite, ν₁(K) ≤ ν₂(K); by symmetry ν₂(K) ≤ ν₁(K). Hence ν₁(K) = ν₂(K) for every compact K.
5. (Agreement on open sets.) By inner regularity on open sets (step 3), for every open O, ν_i(O) = sup{ν_i(K) : K ⊆ O compact}, so ν₁(O) = ν₂(O) by step 4.
6. (Agreement everywhere.) By outer regularity (step 3), for every Borel A, ν_i(A) = inf{ν_i(O) : O ⊇ A open}, so ν₁(A) = ν₂(A) by step 5. Hence ν₁ = ν₂. (Steps 4–6 are exactly the proof of Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported, which applies to the regular measures ν₁, ν₂ because every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) is continuous with compact support, so the hypothesis gives ∫ f dν₁ = ∫ f dν₂.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Finite on compacts ⇒ locally finite on the locally compact space ℝ^P.
Locally finite on the σ-compact metric space ℝ^P ⇒ regular.
Urysohn functions 1_K ≤ f ≤ 1_V and outer regularity give ν₁(K) = ν₂(K) for compact K.
Inner regularity on open sets and outer regularity extend the equality to all Borel sets (Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported).

subproblems.title: Continuity of the rescaled integrals ∫ f d(ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x λ)) in the parameters (x, λ), λ > 0, for a finite μ₀ and continuous compactly supported f (parent step 5a)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ₀ a measure on ℝ^P with μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous with compact support, and x_i ∈ ℝ^P, λ_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ), x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 with x_i → x and λ_i → λ. Then ∫ f d(ofReal(λ_i⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x_i λ_i)) → ∫ f d(ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x λ)) as i → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ₀ : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (xs : ℕ → Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), μ₀ univ ≠ ∞ → Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → (∀ i, 0 < lams i) → 0 < lam → Tendsto xs atTop (𝓝 x) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 lam) → Tendsto (fun i => ∫ v, f v ∂(ENNReal.ofReal ((lams i)⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation (xs i) (lams i)))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ v, f v ∂(ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation x lam))))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 5a (continuity in the parameters via integral_smul_measure, integral_map and dominated convergence), in the sequential form used by parent step 5c and stated for an arbitrary finite measure μ₀.
Notation: η_{a,s} := dilation a s, so η_{a,s}(u) = −(s⁻¹•a) + s⁻¹•u = s⁻¹•(u − a) (definition of dilation and dilationCLM); η_{a,s} is continuous, hence measurable.
1. (Integral formula.) For a ∈ ℝ^P and s > 0: ∫ f d(ofReal(s⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map η_{a,s}) = (ofReal(s⁻¹^n)).toReal·∫ f d(μ₀.map η_{a,s}) (integral_smul_measure) = s⁻¹^n·∫ f(η_{a,s}(v)) dμ₀(v), by ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (s⁻¹^n ≥ 0) and integral_map (η_{a,s} is measurable and f is continuous, hence strongly measurable). We apply this with (a, s) = (x_i, λ_i) and with (a, s) = (x, λ).
2. (Scalar factors.) λ_i → λ ≠ 0, so λ_i⁻¹ → λ⁻¹ (continuity of inversion away from 0; Tendsto.inv₀) and λ_i⁻¹^n → λ⁻¹^n (Tendsto.pow).
3. (Pointwise convergence.) For each v ∈ ℝ^P: η_{x_i,λ_i}(v) = λ_i⁻¹•(v − x_i) → λ⁻¹•(v − x) = η_{x,λ}(v), by step 2, x_i → x and continuity of subtraction and scalar multiplication (Tendsto.sub, Tendsto.smul). Since f is continuous, g_i(v) := f(η_{x_i,λ_i}(v)) → g(v) := f(η_{x,λ}(v)).
4. (Domination.) A continuous function with compact support is bounded: there is C ∈ ℝ with |f(y)| ≤ C for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Hence |g_i(v)| ≤ C for all i and v. The constant C is μ₀-integrable because μ₀ is finite (μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞). Each g_i is continuous (a composition of continuous maps), hence AE-strongly measurable.
5. (Dominated convergence.) By steps 3 and 4 and the dominated convergence theorem (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence), ∫ g_i dμ₀ → ∫ g dμ₀.
6. (Conclusion.) By step 1, the i-th integral equals λ_i⁻¹^n·∫ g_i dμ₀ and the limit integral equals λ⁻¹^n·∫ g dμ₀. By steps 2 and 5 and continuity of multiplication (Tendsto.mul), λ_i⁻¹^n·∫ g_i dμ₀ → λ⁻¹^n·∫ g dμ₀. ∎
proof_key_steps: ∫ f d(ofReal(s⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map η_{a,s}) = s⁻¹^n·∫ f∘η_{a,s} dμ₀ for s > 0.
λ_i⁻¹^n → λ⁻¹^n and f(η_{x_i,λ_i}(v)) → f(η_{x,λ}(v)) pointwise.
f is bounded and μ₀ finite, so dominated convergence gives convergence of ∫ f∘η_{x_i,λ_i} dμ₀; multiply the limits.

subproblems.title: Domain recovery under vague limits: a vague limit of admissible members μ₀^{x_i,λ_i} (μ₀ finite) whose domains all fail to contain a compact K is an admissible member whose domain also fails to contain K (parent step 5c)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and μ₀ a measure on ℝ^P with μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 write μ₀^{x,λ} := ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x λ) and G_{x,λ} := dilation x λ '' B_2(0); call (x, λ) admissible if 0 < λ ≤ 1 and ‖x‖ ≤ 1 − λ. Let (x_i, λ_i) (i ∈ ℕ) be admissible, let ν be a measure on ℝ^P with ν(K') ≠ ∞ for every compact K', such that ∫ f dμ₀^{x_i,λ_i} → ∫ f dν for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, and let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact with K ⊄ G_{x_i,λ_i} for every i. Then there is an admissible (x, λ) with ν = μ₀^{x,λ} and K ⊄ G_{x,λ}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ₀ : Measure (Euclid P)), μ₀ univ ≠ ∞ → ∀ (xs : ℕ → Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (K : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ i, 0 < lams i ∧ lams i ≤ 1 ∧ ‖xs i‖ ≤ 1 - lams i) → (∀ K' : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K' → ν K' ≠ ∞) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun i => ∫ x, f x ∂(ENNReal.ofReal ((lams i)⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation (xs i) (lams i)))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂ν))) → IsCompact K → (∀ i, ¬ K ⊆ dilation (xs i) (lams i) '' ball 0 2) → ∃ (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), (0 < lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ ‖x‖ ≤ 1 - lam) ∧ ν = (ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation x lam)) ∧ ¬ K ⊆ dilation x lam '' ball 0 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 5c (domain recovery; Simon 7.3.3, proof of 3.3(1), items (7) and (9): weak limits of η_{x_i,λ_i#}T with lim λ_i = λ > 0 live on η_{x,λ}(U), chapter-07.txt lines 445–467), stated for an arbitrary finite measure μ₀, which is all that step uses. The parent describes G_{x,λ} as the ball B_{2/λ}(−λ⁻¹x); here the equivalent membership test v ∈ G_{x,λ} ⟺ ‖x + λ•v‖ < 2 of sibling domain_geometry (a) is used (‖v + λ⁻¹x‖ < 2/λ ⟺ ‖x + λv‖ < 2), and the margin argument at the end is the parent's, written for this test. Siblings used: domain_geometry (DG), param_continuity (PC), vague_unique (VU).
1. (Bounding K.) K is compact, hence bounded, so K ⊆ closedBall 0 R₀ for some R₀ ∈ ℝ (IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Put R := max(R₀, 1); then R ≥ 1 > 0 and K ⊆ closedBall 0 R.
2. (Scales bounded below.) For every i, λ_i ≥ R⁻¹. Otherwise λ_i < R⁻¹, so λ_i·R < 1; since (x_i, λ_i) is admissible, DG (c) gives closedBall 0 R ⊆ G_{x_i,λ_i}, hence K ⊆ G_{x_i,λ_i}, contradicting the hypothesis.
3. (Compactness of the parameters.) S := closedBall(0, 1) × [R⁻¹, 1] ⊆ ℝ^P × ℝ is compact (a product of compact sets; closed balls of ℝ^P are compact). Every (x_i, λ_i) lies in S: ‖x_i‖ ≤ 1 − λ_i ≤ 1 and R⁻¹ ≤ λ_i ≤ 1 (step 2 and admissibility). By sequential compactness (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) there are (x*, λ*) ∈ S and a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with (x_{ψ(i)}, λ_{ψ(i)}) → (x*, λ*); applying the continuous projections, x_{ψ(i)} → x* and λ_{ψ(i)} → λ*.
4. (Admissibility of the limit.) (x*, λ*) ∈ S gives λ* ≥ R⁻¹ > 0 and λ* ≤ 1. Both sides of ‖x_{ψ(i)}‖ ≤ 1 − λ_{ψ(i)} converge (continuity of the norm), so in the limit ‖x*‖ ≤ 1 − λ* (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto'). Hence (x*, λ*) is admissible.
5. (Equal integrals.) Let f be continuous with compact support. By PC (μ₀ is finite, λ_{ψ(i)} > 0, λ* > 0, x_{ψ(i)} → x*, λ_{ψ(i)} → λ*), ∫ f dμ₀^{x_{ψ(i)},λ_{ψ(i)}} → ∫ f dμ₀^{x*,λ*}. By hypothesis composed with ψ (ψ(i) → ∞ since ψ is strictly increasing; StrictMono.tendsto_atTop), the same sequence converges to ∫ f dν. Limits in ℝ are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique), so ∫ f dν = ∫ f dμ₀^{x*,λ*}.
6. (ν = μ₀^{x*,λ*}.) ν is finite on compact sets by hypothesis. So is μ₀^{x*,λ*}: for every K', μ₀^{x*,λ*}(K') ≤ μ₀^{x*,λ*}(ℝ^P) = ofReal(λ*⁻¹^n)·μ₀((dilation x* λ*)⁻¹(ℝ^P)) = ofReal(λ*⁻¹^n)·μ₀(ℝ^P) < ∞ (monotonicity; Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply, the dilation being continuous hence measurable). By step 5 and VU (with ν₁ := ν and ν₂ := μ₀^{x*,λ*}), ν = μ₀^{x*,λ*}.
7. (K ⊄ G_{x*,λ*}.) Suppose, for contradiction, that K ⊆ G_{x*,λ*}. K is nonempty: if K = ∅, then K ⊆ G_{x_0,λ_0}, contradicting the hypothesis at i = 0. The function h(v) := ‖x* + λ*•v‖ is continuous, so it attains its maximum M = h(v₀) on the nonempty compact set K (IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn). As v₀ ∈ K ⊆ G_{x*,λ*}, DG (a) (λ* > 0) gives M < 2. Put γ := 2 − M > 0. By step 3 there is an index i with ‖x_{ψ(i)} − x*‖ < γ/2 and |λ_{ψ(i)} − λ*| < γ/(2R) (each holds for all large i; Metric.tendsto_nhds). For every v ∈ K we have ‖v‖ ≤ R (step 1) and h(v) ≤ M, and x_{ψ(i)} + λ_{ψ(i)}•v = (x* + λ*•v) + (x_{ψ(i)} − x*) + (λ_{ψ(i)} − λ*)•v, so by the triangle inequality ‖x_{ψ(i)} + λ_{ψ(i)}•v‖ ≤ M + ‖x_{ψ(i)} − x*‖ + |λ_{ψ(i)} − λ*|·R < M + γ/2 + γ/2 = 2. By DG (a) (λ_{ψ(i)} > 0), v ∈ G_{x_{ψ(i)},λ_{ψ(i)}}. Hence K ⊆ G_{x_{ψ(i)},λ_{ψ(i)}}, contradicting the hypothesis at the index ψ(i). Therefore K ⊄ G_{x*,λ*}.
8. (Conclusion.) (x, λ) := (x*, λ*) is admissible (step 4), ν = μ₀^{x,λ} (step 6) and K ⊄ G_{x,λ} (step 7). ∎
proof_key_steps: K ⊆ closedBall 0 R with R ≥ 1; by domain_geometry (c), K ⊄ G_{x_i,λ_i} forces λ_i ≥ 1/R.
The admissible parameters with λ ≥ 1/R lie in the compact set closedBall(0,1) × [1/R, 1]; extract a convergent subsequence with admissible limit (x*, λ*).
param_continuity and uniqueness of limits give ∫ f dν = ∫ f dμ₀^{x*,λ*}; both are finite on compacts, so vague_unique gives ν = μ₀^{x*,λ*}.
If K ⊆ G_{x*,λ*}, the maximum M < 2 of ‖x* + λ*v‖ on K and convergence of the parameters give ‖x_{ψ(i)} + λ_{ψ(i)}v‖ < 2 on K for some i, i.e. K ⊆ G_{x_{ψ(i)},λ_{ψ(i)}}, a contradiction.

subproblems.title: n-homogeneity of f·Hⁿ for a dilation-invariant density f (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] an arbitrary function (no measurability assumed), and λ > 0 with f(λx) = f(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Let ν := H^n.withDensity f. Then for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P, ν(λA) = λ^n·ν(A), where λA = (x ↦ λx)(A) is the image of A; in [0, ∞] this reads ν(λA) = ofReal(λ^n)·ν(A).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → (∀ x : Euclid P, f (lam • x) = f x) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f ((fun x => lam • x) '' A) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam ^ n) * (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dimred_cs_mi_withDensity_dilate of DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.cone_splitting-a1.measure_invariance-a1.dilate_homogeneity-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit fc55b7480dccf7e48261ad5b085ddd0c0cc9f1d6). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node; registering it here overlays its accepted candidate history (which already contains its own accepted dependency Submission.euclid_hausdorff_dilation_change_of_variables) for the sibling nonhomogeneous, which lists it in depends_on. It is also already a registered dependency of the selected node. Use under the selected node: the sibling nonhomogeneous (parent step 6) applies it with λ := t > 0 and A := B_1(0) to obtain (Hⁿ.withDensity f)(B_t(0)) = ofReal(t^n)·(Hⁿ.withDensity f)(B_1(0)). The numbered proof below is that node's independently reviewed parent-supplied proof, reproduced unchanged; its 'parent'/'sibling' references are to that node's own parent and siblings.

Source: step 7 of the parent proof (homogeneity (ii)), with the density function ofReal ∘ Θ replaced by an arbitrary f satisfying f(λ·) = f. The change of variables ∫_{λA} g dH^n = λ^n ∫_A g(λw) dH^n(w) used there is the sibling dilation_change_of_variables (the reused accepted declaration Submission.euclid_hausdorff_dilation_change_of_variables, which step 7 cites).
Notation: δ(x) := λx on ℝ^P, H^n = μHE[n], ν := H^n.withDensity f, and D := δ(A) = λA.
1. δ is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse x ↦ λ⁻¹x (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ, λ ≠ 0). Hence δ is a measurable embedding and injective. So D = δ(A) is Borel (the image of a Borel set under a measurable embedding), and δ⁻¹(D) = A by injectivity.
2. Apply part (ii) of the sibling dilation_change_of_variables with c := λ > 0, M := D and g := f. It gives ∫⁻_{δ⁻¹(D)} f(λz) dH^n(z) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) · ∫⁻_D f dH^n; it holds for every f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞].
3. By step 1, δ⁻¹(D) = A, and by hypothesis f(λz) = f(z) for every z. So step 2 becomes ∫⁻_A f dH^n = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) · ∫⁻_D f dH^n.
4. A and D are Borel, so ν(A) = ∫⁻_A f dH^n and ν(D) = ∫⁻_D f dH^n (withDensity_apply). Hence ν(A) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) · ν(D).
5. Multiply both sides by ofReal(λ^n). Since λ^n ≥ 0 and λ⁻¹^n ≥ 0, ofReal(λ^n) · ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) = ofReal(λ^n · λ⁻¹^n) = ofReal((λ · λ⁻¹)^n) = ofReal(1) = 1, using λ ≠ 0. Therefore ofReal(λ^n) · ν(A) = ν(D) = ν(λA). ∎
proof_key_steps: x ↦ λx is a homeomorphism, so λA is Borel and (λ·)⁻¹(λA) = A.
The reused change of variables (sibling dilation_change_of_variables) with g = f and f(λ·) = f gives ν(A) = λ^{-n} ν(λA).
Multiplying by ofReal(λ^n) gives ν(λA) = ofReal(λ^n)·ν(A).

subproblems.title: A measure of finite positive total mass is not of the form Hⁿ.withDensity f with f(t·w) = f(w) for all t > 0, when n ≥ 1 (parent step 6)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, ν a measure on ℝ^P with ν(ℝ^P) ≠ 0 and ν(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞, and f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] an arbitrary function (no measurability assumed) with f(t·w) = f(w) for every t > 0 and w ∈ ℝ^P. Then ν ≠ μHE[n].withDensity f.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞), 1 ≤ n → ν univ ≠ 0 → ν univ ≠ ∞ → (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∀ w : Euclid P, f (t • w) = f w) → ν ≠ (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 6 (non-homogeneity), stated for an arbitrary measure ν of finite positive total mass. In the parent, ν := μ₀^{x,λ}, whose total mass lies in (0, ∞) by the sibling total_mass; this gives clause (6). Sibling used: withdensity_dilate (WD), the accepted Submission.dimred_cs_mi_withDensity_dilate.
Notation: ρ := μHE[n].withDensity f.
1. Suppose, for contradiction, that ν = ρ. Then ρ(ℝ^P) ≠ 0 and ρ(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞.
2. (Scaling of balls.) Let t > 0. The hypothesis gives f(t•w) = f(w) for every w, and B_1(0) is Borel, so WD (with λ := t and A := B_1(0)) gives ρ((w ↦ t•w) '' B_1(0)) = ofReal(t^n)·ρ(B_1(0)). The image (w ↦ t•w) '' B_1(0) = t•B_1(0) equals B_{‖t‖}(0) = B_t(0) (Set.image_smul, smul_unitBall, ‖t‖ = t). Hence ρ(B_t(0)) = ofReal(t^n)·ρ(B_1(0)) for every t > 0.
3. (Case ρ(B_1(0)) = 0.) Then ρ(B_t(0)) = 0 for every t > 0 by step 2. Every v ∈ ℝ^P lies in B_{m+1}(0) for a natural number m > ‖v‖ (Archimedean property), so ℝ^P = ⋃_{m ∈ ℕ} B_{m+1}(0), and by countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null) ρ(ℝ^P) = 0, contradicting step 1.
4. (Case ρ(B_1(0)) ≠ 0.) For t ≥ 1 we have t^n ≥ t^1 = t (n ≥ 1; pow_le_pow_right₀), so by monotonicity of ofReal and of ρ and by step 2: ofReal(t)·ρ(B_1(0)) ≤ ofReal(t^n)·ρ(B_1(0)) = ρ(B_t(0)) ≤ ρ(ℝ^P). Moreover ofReal(t) → ∞ as t → ∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal_atTop), so ofReal(t)·ρ(B_1(0)) → ∞·ρ(B_1(0)) (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const, applicable because the limit ∞ is ≠ 0), and ∞·ρ(B_1(0)) = ∞ because ρ(B_1(0)) ≠ 0 (ENNReal.top_mul). Since these values are ≤ ρ(ℝ^P) for all t ≥ 1, the limit satisfies ∞ ≤ ρ(ℝ^P) (le_of_tendsto), i.e. ρ(ℝ^P) = ∞, contradicting step 1.
5. Both cases are impossible, so ν ≠ ρ = μHE[n].withDensity f. ∎
proof_key_steps: withdensity_dilate with A = B_1(0) and t•B_1(0) = B_t(0) gives ρ(B_t(0)) = ofReal(t^n)·ρ(B_1(0)) for ρ = Hⁿ.withDensity f.
If ρ(B_1(0)) = 0, all balls about 0 are null and ρ(ℝ^P) = 0.
Either way ρ(ℝ^P) ∈ {0, ∞}, whereas ν(ℝ^P) ∈ (0, ∞); so ν ≠ ρ.

subproblems.title: Transferred lower mass bound for the members μ₀^{x,λ} on balls whose closure lies in their domain (parent steps 0(c)–(e), 7)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, z ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0 and μ₀ := ofReal(r⁻¹^n)•(μ⌞B_{2r}(z)).map(dilation z r); for x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 let μ₀^{x,λ} := ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x λ) and G_{x,λ} := dilation x λ '' B_2(0). Let Λ₀ ≥ 0 and suppose that ofReal(e^{−(Λ₀σ)})·(ω_n·ofReal(σ^n)) ≤ μ(B_σ(p)) whenever p ∈ ℝ^P satisfies μ(B_ε(p)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0, closedBall p ρ' ⊆ closedBall z (2r) and 0 < σ < ρ' (ω_n = unitBallVolume n). Then for all x, y ∈ ℝ^P, 0 < λ ≤ 1 and ρ > 0 with closedBall y ρ ⊆ G_{x,λ} and μ₀^{x,λ}(B_ε(y)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0: ofReal(e^{−(r·Λ₀·ρ)})·(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) ≤ μ₀^{x,λ}(B_ρ(y)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ μ₀ : Measure (Euclid P)) (z : Euclid P) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → μ₀ = ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) • (μ.restrict (ball z (2 * r))).map (dilation z r) → ∀ Λ₀ : ℝ, 0 ≤ Λ₀ → (∀ p : Euclid P, (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → μ (ball p ε) ≠ 0) → ∀ σ ρ : ℝ, closedBall p ρ ⊆ closedBall z (2 * r) → 0 < σ → σ < ρ → ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-(Λ₀ * σ))) * (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (σ ^ n)) ≤ μ (ball p σ)) → ∀ (x y : Euclid P) (lam ρ : ℝ), 0 < lam → lam ≤ 1 → 0 < ρ → closedBall y ρ ⊆ dilation x lam '' ball 0 2 → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → (ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation x lam)) (ball y ε) ≠ 0) → ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-(r * Λ₀ * ρ))) * (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)) ≤ (ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation x lam)) (ball y ρ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 7 (transferred lower bound), with the ball formula of parent steps 0(c)–(e) proved inline (the parent's sibling ambient_calculus is not available to this child), and the membership test of the sibling domain_geometry (DG) (a) used for the containment of parent step 0(e). This is clause (7) of the parent; the parent hypotheses n ≥ 1 and μ(B_{2r}(z)) ∈ (0, ∞) are not needed.
Notation: B := B_{2r}(z); η_{a,t} := dilation a t, so η_{a,t}(u) = −(t⁻¹•a) + t⁻¹•u = t⁻¹•(u − a), a continuous, hence measurable, map; s := rλ > 0; p := z + r•(x + λ•y); ω_n := unitBallVolume n.
1. (Preimages of balls.) For a, w ∈ ℝ^P, t > 0 and σ ∈ ℝ: η_{a,t}⁻¹(B_σ(w)) = B_{tσ}(a + t•w), because t⁻¹•(v − a) − w = t⁻¹•(v − (a + t•w)) and t⁻¹‖v − (a + t•w)‖ < σ ⟺ ‖v − (a + t•w)‖ < tσ.
2. (Ball formula.) For every σ ∈ ℝ: μ₀^{x,λ}(B_σ(y)) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·μ₀(η_{x,λ}⁻¹(B_σ(y))) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·μ₀(B_{λσ}(x + λ•y)) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·(ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·μ(η_{z,r}⁻¹(B_{λσ}(x + λ•y)) ∩ B)) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·(ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·μ(B_{sσ}(p) ∩ B)), by Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply (balls are Borel), step 1 twice (r(λσ) = sσ), and Measure.restrict_apply.
3. (Containment.) closedBall p (sρ) ⊆ B. Let q ∈ closedBall p (sρ) and u := y + s⁻¹•(q − p). Then ‖u − y‖ = s⁻¹‖q − p‖ ≤ ρ, so u ∈ closedBall y ρ ⊆ G_{x,λ}, and DG (a) gives ‖x + λ•u‖ < 2. Since λs⁻¹ = r⁻¹, x + λ•u = x + λ•y + r⁻¹•(q − p) = x + λ•y + r⁻¹•(q − z) − (x + λ•y) = r⁻¹•(q − z). Hence r⁻¹‖q − z‖ < 2, i.e. ‖q − z‖ < 2r, so q ∈ B.
4. (Ball formula without intersection.) For σ ≤ ρ: B_{sσ}(p) ⊆ closedBall p (sσ) ⊆ closedBall p (sρ) ⊆ B (step 3), so B_{sσ}(p) ∩ B = B_{sσ}(p) and μ₀^{x,λ}(B_σ(y)) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·(ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·μ(B_{sσ}(p))).
5. (p ∈ spt μ.) Let ε' > 0 and σ := min(ρ, ε'/s) > 0. By hypothesis μ₀^{x,λ}(B_σ(y)) ≠ 0, so by step 4 μ(B_{sσ}(p)) ≠ 0 (a product with a zero factor vanishes). Since sσ ≤ ε', B_{sσ}(p) ⊆ B_{ε'}(p) and μ(B_{ε'}(p)) ≠ 0 (measure_mono_null).
6. (Margin.) closedBall p (sρ) is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and contained in the open set B (step 3), so there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ (closedBall p (sρ)) ⊆ B (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). In a real normed space cthickening δ (closedBall p (sρ)) = closedBall p (δ + sρ) (cthickening_closedBall; δ ≥ 0, sρ ≥ 0); directly, a point q with ‖q − p‖ ≤ sρ already lies in closedBall p (sρ), and a point q with sρ < ‖q − p‖ ≤ sρ + δ is within distance ‖q − p‖ − sρ ≤ δ of the point p + (sρ/‖q − p‖)(q − p) of closedBall p (sρ). Hence closedBall p (sρ + δ) ⊆ B ⊆ closedBall z (2r).
7. (Lower bound for μ.) Apply the hypothesis on μ at the point p (step 5) with σ := sρ and ρ' := sρ + δ: closedBall p ρ' ⊆ closedBall z (2r) (step 6) and 0 < sρ < sρ + δ. It gives ofReal(e^{−(Λ₀·sρ)})·(ω_n·ofReal((sρ)^n)) ≤ μ(B_{sρ}(p)).
8. (Rescaling.) Since λ⁻¹^n, r⁻¹^n and (sρ)^n are ≥ 0, ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·(ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·ofReal((sρ)^n)) = ofReal((λ⁻¹r⁻¹·rλ)^n·ρ^n) = ofReal(ρ^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, mul_pow, λ⁻¹r⁻¹rλ = 1). Multiplying the inequality of step 7 by ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·ofReal(r⁻¹^n) and using step 4 with σ = ρ gives ofReal(e^{−(Λ₀·sρ)})·(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) ≤ ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·(ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·μ(B_{sρ}(p))) = μ₀^{x,λ}(B_ρ(y)).
9. (Comparing exponents.) Λ₀·sρ = Λ₀rλρ ≤ rΛ₀ρ, because Λ₀rρ ≥ 0 and λ ≤ 1. Hence −(rΛ₀ρ) ≤ −(Λ₀sρ), e^{−(r·Λ₀·ρ)} ≤ e^{−(Λ₀sρ)} (Real.exp_le_exp) and ofReal(e^{−(r·Λ₀·ρ)}) ≤ ofReal(e^{−(Λ₀sρ)}) (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal). Multiplying by ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) and combining with step 8 gives ofReal(e^{−(r·Λ₀·ρ)})·(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) ≤ μ₀^{x,λ}(B_ρ(y)). ∎
proof_key_steps: μ₀^{x,λ}(B_σ(y)) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)·ofReal(r⁻¹^n)·μ(B_{rλσ}(p) ∩ B_{2r}(z)) with p = z + r(x + λy).
closedBall y ρ ⊆ G_{x,λ} and the membership test of domain_geometry give closedBall p (rλρ) ⊆ B_{2r}(z), so the intersection drops for σ ≤ ρ and p ∈ spt μ.
Compactness gives a margin δ > 0 with closedBall p (rλρ + δ) ⊆ closedBall z (2r); the hypothesis on μ at p with σ = rλρ applies.
Rescaling by ofReal((rλ)⁻ⁿ) and e^{−rΛ₀ρ} ≤ e^{−Λ₀rλρ} (λ ≤ 1) give the bound.
